audit_scope: Read-only classification of complete retrieved Fabric Feeds and Geo/Map Layers catalogs; not runtime selection or current access certification.
methodology: Read every collected UTF-8 content string, verify recorded byte length and strictly parse YAML frontmatter without silently accepting duplicate keys.
Select actual kind:record notes in the two catalog directories; exclude exact host/index pages and .base views. Preserve the explicit older top-level-copy record.
Assign one analyst role and primary intended-delivery class per row; keep secondary classes. Categories are interpretations of text, not current source availability or unique-provider totals.
Retain raw metadata/Markdown, exact paths/IDs/URLs, SHA-256 and field line evidence for every row. Do not silently normalize malformed or mismatched source tokens.
Endpoint classification uses only the provided URL syntax/context, never HTTP checks. A machine-looking path is a candidate, not proof of access, correct format, license or completeness.
Status/access/auth/origin/client labels are historical metadata. All 240 records have no observed runtime health; no network tests or purchases performed.
The other 21 retrieved files provide context and requirements evidence, not additional Fabric Feeds/Map Layers record counts. Original migration manifest was not retrieved.

role_definitions.source_or_dataset_candidate: Catalog identifies a candidate upstream dataset/provider, but readiness and exact machine access are not established. This is not a count of accessible sources.
role_definitions.website_or_dashboard_only: The named offering/link is a map, UI, homepage or narrative website with no evidenced export contract in the row; API labels alone are not proof.
role_definitions.hosted_service_or_platform: Geocoding/query/hosting/tiling platform or catalogued self-hosted service; concrete dataset/asset/request selection needed.
role_definitions.protocol_or_standard: Device/network/protocol or file-format specification, not an independently accessible upstream source.
role_definitions.tool_or_adapter: Software, client, editor, recorder or translation adapter, not an independent data provider.
role_definitions.catalog_or_reference: Discovery portal, dataset directory or system reference; a more specific dataset/service must be selected.
role_definitions.commercial_platform_reference: North Star paid/composite product feature claims with UI/marketing URLs only; export/API entitlement not established.

delivery_class_definitions.live_entities: Intended moving/contact/station-state telemetry, including derived orbital positions and protocol capability; does not certify a realtime stream.
delivery_class_definitions.event_alert_features: Geolocated events/alerts, time-varying polygons or environmental observations; includes historical batches and sensor samples, not only realtime alerts.
delivery_class_definitions.raster_vector_imagery: Raster/vector tiles, imagery assets, map/terrain rendering services or related format/reference capability; keep separate from per-feature event buses.
delivery_class_definitions.static_overlays: Fixed/slow-changing infrastructure, boundaries, inventories, reference features or lookup output.
delivery_class_definitions.media: Audio/video/camera streams or media capture inputs; metadata/markers and actual media transport are separate.
delivery_class_definitions.non_geospatial_reference: Finance, cyber, social/news, reference/enrichment, tools/clients or composite platform references without direct geolocated feature contract.

gap_definitions.historical_not_runtime: Status/auth/access/origin/client labels are exported historical metadata; no current network, deployment, account or permission test performed.
gap_definitions.source_control_missing: No explicit source_enabled state, stop/start API, drain/restart/catch-up policy or scoped authorization in this record.
gap_definitions.tak_control_missing: No independent TAK publication enabled state, audience/mission policy, actual sink or CoT/layer contract in this record.
gap_definitions.local_visibility_missing: No per-user/device view visibility state or independence contract in this record.
gap_definitions.credential_contract_missing: Auth type is present but no credential reference, scope, issuer/renewal or entitled dataset; None is not verified anonymous access.
gap_definitions.request_contract_missing: No executable request/stream subscription contract including method, headers/query, geofence, schedule, limits and response validation.
gap_definitions.schema_identity_freshness_missing: No normalized schema version, concrete source/entity IDs, provenance, units/CRS/accuracy, event-time lifecycle or freshness/expiry contract.
gap_definitions.concrete_nats_subject_missing: No concrete publish subject; either catalog subject absent or only wildcard/angle-bracket template.
gap_definitions.rate_or_cadence_missing: No notion_rate_limit field; throughput quota and refresh cadence still need separate definitions.
gap_definitions.rate_label_not_contract: notion_rate_limit mixes cadence/quotas/qualitative assertions; not an executable scheduler or verified provider limit.
gap_definitions.non_source_record: Specification, tool, platform or discovery reference; not one independent ready-to-run upstream feed.
gap_definitions.only_ui_evidence: Recorded link is a UI/homepage or product reference, not a documented export/stream contract.
gap_definitions.license_reuse_unverified: Free/Paid/etc is not a verified license, permission to redistribute/cache, or account entitlement.
gap_definitions.layer_or_asset_missing: No selected service sublayer, query, style/TileJSON, tile matrix, imagery asset/date or client-ready artifact is defined.

Two map records share exact service URL; feed points at another ArcGIS hostname for World_Imagery. Canonical service/layer review needed.
Observation/alert collection, radar/weather tiles and embed UI are different interfaces/deliverables; quota/keys and enabled state cannot be inferred from provider alone.
Keyed thermal detections API versus map overlay/service; interface-specific entitlement and lifecycle.
Exact same FeatureServer URL, collection vs map publication.
Different sensor networks and sampling semantics, some shared subjects, several webpage-only links.
WRI exact same dataset URL is collection/display overlap; EIA is a different dataset.
Public vs self-hosted lookup/query services; DeFlock is a derived fixed-infrastructure dataset, not a raw surveillance-hit feed.
Twelve separate catalog records describing six product/interface concepts across collection/display catalogs, not twelve proven APIs or 45+ additional verified upstreams.

issues_and_ambiguities.finding: Fabric Feeds host index states 160 nested rows; directory contains 161 kind:record notes: 160 notion_database=Fabric Feeds plus one explicitly preserved older top-level-copy LiveUAMap. No row dropped. Map Layers host count 79 matches.
issues_and_ambiguities.resolution: Explained by preserved copy metadata/body; original migration manifest was not among the 265 retrieved files, so manifest-level reconciliation was not performed.

issues_and_ambiguities.finding: Three casefold-title duplicate groups, seven rows, all distinct IDs. LiveUAMap has three conflicting historical versions; two other names repeat across catalogs. Preserve identities and review canonical dataset mappings before activation.

75 records marked Live, 148 Planned, one Testing, 16 Reference; generic status active on every row. None is current runtime proof. Examples include MTA zero-replica origin/Testing vs Planned and ACLED map Live vs feed Planned.
USPTO Patents source_url is an api.usaspending.gov search URL. The provider identity and link disagree; original value preserved, no correction guessed.

Homepage, dashboard, product fragment, protocol and API Key labels do not establish usable exports. North Star 250k-camera/45+-feed/AI/fusion claims remain descriptive and unverified, not additional catalog records.

Auth labels conflict across versions/interfaces or supplemental notes; Free/Gov/Open is not a current entitlement. Military/classified integration, paid surveillance and subscriptions need separate authorization gates.

149 feed subjects present, but 145 contain * and five contain angle-bracket placeholders (overlap one). Zero concrete publish subjects are specified. Eight repeated subject groups also need per-source provenance and agreed namespaces.

No catalog record defines independent source-enabled, TAK-publication-enabled or local-visibility state. Existing /ops/feeds note says toggle on/off but does not assign control scope; overlay toggle notes describe local rendering.

No row provides configured secret reference or typed schema/freshness/identity contract; 84 feeds omit rate-limit metadata. 226 of 240 bodies are explicitly title-only. Catalog is scope inventory, not deployable pipeline definitions.
Protocols, hardware capabilities, adapters, style editors and desktop clients must not be counted as independent upstream providers; they may need separate hardware/local runtimes or serving paths.

TLE requires propagation; imagery needs asset/catalog delivery; station infrastructure differs from incidents; camera marker metadata differs from audio/video; internal service DNS differs from client-ready access.

One architecture note says TAK-only/no custom dashboards; frontend-overlap note recommends WWV global globe and local layer toggles. Do not infer a current frontend/runtime decision. Decouple collection, publication, rendering and reasoning.
Unofficial/HTTP tile templates, self-hosted tailnet addresses and cluster-local DNS need explicit rights, security and access-route validation; no endpoint tests were permitted or performed.

source_enabled.effect: Whether new upstream collection and normalized ingestion run. Off pauses new fetch/stream work per drain policy; it does not delete history or local caches.
source_enabled.must_not_imply: TAK delivery or any user visibility; enabling a publisher does not implicitly enable collection.
source_enabled.evidence: Recommended separation inferred from S01/S03/S04; no explicit state field in catalog.

tak_publish_enabled.scope: dataset/interface publication per mission/audience or TAK sink
tak_publish_enabled.effect: Whether eligible normalized data is converted/forwarded or an appropriate TAK layer/data-package is published. Off leaves upstream collection, durable storage and other authorized consumers running. Existing tracks use explicit stale/withdraw policy.
tak_publish_enabled.must_not_imply: Source off or local hidden. No stale-backlog emission merely because toggle turned on.
tak_publish_enabled.evidence: S03 CoT bridge, data package and Network Link KML are distinct delivery options; historical integration label is not enablement.

local_visibility.effect: Whether this client renders/subscribes to a layer. May stop that client fetching tiles, not the shared source. Existing persisted preferences remain local unless deliberately shared.
local_visibility.must_not_imply: Collection paused or TAK publishing disabled for other clients.
local_visibility.evidence: S05 layer-toggle/global-globe notes and S06 KMZ-group toggles demonstrate rendering requirements; S01 does not define this scope.

recommended_acceptance_criteria.criterion: All 240 retrieved records remain traceable by immutable Notion ID/path. Alias/overlap groups resolve to reviewed canonical provider/dataset/interface IDs without deleting history or counting software as data. Quarantine the USPTO/USAspending mismatch; retain unresolved older LiveUAMap until approved.

Before activation, each real dataset has approved license/coverage/AOI, exact request or subscription (method/URL/query/headers/topics/filter), documented format/schema and current expected response, provider quota distinct from poll cadence, secret reference/scope/renewal, owning operator and network/hardware dependency. Paid, restricted and sensitive sources default blocked pending authorization.

Demonstrate with authorized fixtures and then scoped pilot data: polled JSON/GeoJSON hazards, WebSocket AIS, GTFS-RT protobuf plus static GTFS enrichment, APRS TCP or MQTT telemetry, STAC/raster/vector tile delivery, static feature/KMZ delivery and media metadata. RF capture/ASR/orbit propagation may be separate jobs; prove integration rather than assuming one engine natively handles them.

Versioned envelope preserves canonical source/provider IDs, upstream entity/event IDs, event/observed/ingested times, geometry with CRS/altitude reference/accuracy, units, quality and provenance. Distinguish moving entity state, alert revisions/cancellation, historical batches, fixed POIs, media and imagery. Define original-event-time freshness/TTL per class; reject invalid coordinates and avoid invented geolocation.

Bound per-provider retries/backoff/rate budgets and queues; isolate slow or malformed feeds; quarantine poison messages with replay provenance. Prove reconnect/restart, checkpointed resumption, provider outages, duplicate deliveries, out-of-order updates and sink outage recovery. Idempotent source+event/revision handling must preserve changed positions under the same entity UID and never replay expired alerts as fresh.

Persist source_enabled globally per canonical collector/dataset; persist tak_publish_enabled per publication/mission/audience; store local_visibility per user/device/view. No checkbox implicitly changes another scope. Test source on/TAK off, source on/TAK on/local hidden, source off/visible, and re-enable after restart. Define drain, in-flight cutoff, catch-up, expiration/withdrawal and existing-track behavior. TAK not applicable is explicit for non-geospatial/reference rows.

For tracks/events, validate stable UIDs, correct source-derived affiliations/types, times, stale policy and geometry against target clients. For large/static/raster data, test WMS/WMTS/XYZ, feature/KML network-link or data-package paths as applicable instead of forcing all items into CoT points. Validate selected layers/styles/assets, EPSG:4326/3857 transforms, tile matrices, bounds, attribution and authorized device access. If local UI only mirrors TAK, explain why TAK-disabled data cannot appear there without a separate local data path.

Show desired vs effective source/publisher state separately from local visibility; show last successful fetch, upstream event age, errors/rate limiting, collection/publication counters and backlog per source and sink. Apply scoped authorization, change audit, rollback and sensitive-data retention. Local hide must not stop collection/history/AI or hide data on another device.

Only after dataset contracts and workload volumes are known, score candidate platforms against these acceptance tests, operating model and measured resource/cost limits. Historical notes advocating Redpanda or a frontend do not count as current product verification. This audit makes no n8n/Node-RED/Redpanda runtime selection.

# DeFlock — Crowdsourced ALPR / License Plate Reader Map

# ⚡ Zeus Intelligence Notes — Surveillance Evolution
> The trajectory of surveillance is away from cameras toward invisible, distributed sensor fusion. DeFlock maps today's visible infrastructure — what's coming has no lens.
## The Sensor Evolution Chain
```plain text
LICENSE PLATES
      ↓
    VIDEO (CCTV, Flock, ANPR)
      ↓
    BLUETOOTH (device MAC scanning)
      ↓
    RF (WiFi probes, IMSI catchers, passive SDR)
      ↓
    DRONES (aerial surveillance + sensor fusion)
      ↓
    FUSION ← NEW SENSORS → NEW DATABASE
         (no single system — everything talks to everything)
```
## The Shift: No Camera — Pure RF Sensor
> The next generation of surveillance has no lens. RF sensors are smaller, cheaper, hidden, and passive. They leave no visible footprint and require no line-of-sight.
- RF sensors detect device signatures without a camera — no image, no privacy trigger, no obvious hardware
- Smaller than a smoke detector — can be embedded in street furniture, utility boxes, signage
- Completely passive — emits nothing, only listens — nearly undetectable
- No maintenance, no lens to clean, no light requirement — works day/night/fog
- Reads: WiFi probe requests, Bluetooth advertisements, IMSI (cell), tire pressure sensors (TPMS), key fobs, AirTags
## What Gets Tracked — PLATE · TIME · PLACE · ROUTE
```plain text
PLATE     → vehicle identity (ALPR)
TIME      → when you were there (timestamp)
PLACE     → where you were (GPS/cell sector)
ROUTE     → where you came from + where you went (correlated across nodes)

Together = pattern of life. Not just where you are — where you always are.
```
## Fusion: The Person Behind the Vehicle
> The vehicle is just the first node. Fusion correlates the vehicle to the person inside it using every sensor they carry on their body.
- PHONE — WiFi probe + Bluetooth MAC + IMSI + app location pings = device fingerprint tied to vehicle plate
- WATCH — Bluetooth LE advertisement (Apple Watch, Garmin, Fitbit) — unique device ID broadcast continuously
- EARBUDS — Bluetooth broadcast (AirPods, Galaxy Buds) — additional corroborating device signature
- TIRE SENSORS — TPMS (Tire Pressure Monitoring System) broadcasts a unique ID on 315/433MHz RF — passive readers already deployed at some intersections and border crossings
- Fusion: plate + phone MAC + watch BLE + TPMS ID = individual person, not just vehicle
- Cross-reference across nodes = full route reconstruction of person, not just car
## The Future: No Cameras — Just Sensors
> The end state is a world where surveillance infrastructure is invisible. No cameras. No lenses. Just a silent RF mesh that knows where everyone is, was, and will be.
- Passive RF mesh — no active emission, no visible hardware, no legal 'camera' to regulate
- Every device a person carries becomes a beacon — opt-out is physically removing the device
- New database paradigm — not 'we have footage of you' but 'we have your signature across 400 nodes'
- TPMS unique IDs mean even a rental car with a burner phone is traceable if the tires are stock
- The countermeasure is hardware removal, not covering a lens — fundamentally different threat model
## OneMind Relevance
- DeFlock today maps the visible layer — the ALPR cameras Zeus can see and document
- The OneMind fabric should model the invisible layer too — TPMS readers, BLE scanners, IMSI catchers on the map
- Fabric Feeds: fabric.intel.surveillance.alpr.* → extend to fabric.intel.surveillance.rf.*
- TAK overlay: not just cameras as CoT points — RF sensor nodes, TPMS readers, BLE mesh as separate intel layer
- Fusion engine on NATS: correlate plate + device + TPMS hits across time → pattern of life stream
---
